react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten differentially abundant metabolites are resolved to ChEBI with consistent InChIKey block-14 validation and no structural conflicts. Cross-paradigm pathway analysis using run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA), run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA), and run_mummichog (m/z-direct empirical network) converges on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the overwhelming top hit: RaMP FDR 5.56e-18 with 7 of 10 input metabolites, MetaboAnalystR p=1.59e-08 with 6 metabolites, and Mummichog p=0.00143 with near-complete 17-of-18 overlap. The RaMP ranked pathway also captures Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.38e-08) and Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.46e-10). Mummichog additionally surfaces Arginine and Proline Metabolism (p=0.0286) driven by 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912) and its hydroxylated analogue (C04281), but this ranks far below the tryptophan signal. L-Valine (C00183) appears as a single-hit outlier in KEGG:hsa00290 (Valine metabolism, p=0.0444) and does not connect to the tryptophan axis. The driver metabolites L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and quinolinic acid (C03722) together span the complete tryptophan degradation cascade from substrate to neuroactive derivatives and the kynurenine-branch NAD+ precursor. The treatment perturbation selectively alters tryptophan catabolism with a coherent signal across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms.

RaMP enrichment returns KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 0 with FDR 5.56e-18, and WikiPathways WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR 1.73e-14. The kynurenine-branch pathway WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production) ranks 4 with FDR 1.46e-10, and the IDO metabolic pathway WP:WP5414 ranks 8 with FDR 1.36e-08. Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) ranks 9 with FDR 3.38e-08. Seven metabolites appear in KEGG:map00380 including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine, and indoleacetaldehyde. Four metabolites appear in the kynurenine-branch WP:WP4210: L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, serotonin, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. L-Valine appears in the broader metabolism super-pathway REACT:R-HSA-71291 but not in the tryptophan-specific pathways. The convergence across ORA methods and the specificity of the hit list indicates a coherent perturbation of tryptophan catabolism with effects on both neuroactive derivatives and NAD+ precursor production.
